revision.asymmetry: This revision contains ONLY changes that make the verdict STRICTER or are verdict-neutral clarifications. It contains ZERO changes that make passing easier. Sections 3.1/3.2/3.4/3.5/3.6 (criteria, thresholds, feature sets, tests) are UNCHANGED from version 1.
corrections: n=5 freeze is WITHDRAWN: the confirmatory n is frozen AFTER the pilot (preregistration.md 2.4). It was a convention, not a power calculation.
'Tier 0/1 cannot be started before the freeze is lifted' was WRONG: they are computable entirely offline from the existing NDJSON (preregistration.md 5-3).
additions: 2.1 rewritten: argumentative writing is the BEST CASE for keystrokes, not a representative task
2.8 pilot clause (researcher, excluded from the confirmatory sample)
3.7 asymmetry of conclusions and the concrete next action when the result is negative
3.8 ecological validity limits (G1 is a floor check on measurability)
3.9 n=1 handling: exhaustive enumeration, Fisher only for n>=2
5.1 handling of zero-variance features (feature set unchanged)
clarification_only: 3.3-3 denominator expressed as a FRACTION (>=80% of n) instead of '4 of 5'. Neither 80% nor AUC 0.60 changed.

design.rationale_block_count: C(8,4)=70 permutations -> min exact p = 1/70 = 0.0143 < 0.05. With 4 blocks C(4,2)=6 -> min p = 0.167, unreachable.
design.rationale_copy_block_position: Keeps the forced-comparison chain closed inside the 8 G1 blocks (a copy block between two G1 blocks would break 'compared with the previous block'). Also makes the leading copy block serve as the individual transcription baseline [P38].
design.domain_rationale: Argumentative writing is chosen because it is the BEST CASE for keystroke observation, NOT because it is representative. VibeCoding has thin continuous typing (ADR-006 sub-decision 3) and Creative is typing-sparse with silence indistinguishable from idle. G1 settles the question on the most favourable ground: a floor check. Representativeness is NOT claimed; participant P011 stated in F4 that they rarely write continuously.

n_subjects_rule.why_withdrawn: n=5 was a convention ('same size as Phase1'), not a power calculation (decisions.md judgement 8). The primary test is WITHIN-subject: C(8,4)=70 means n=1 already reaches min p=0.0143<0.05. The required n depends on the DIRECTION of the result, which cannot be known in advance: separation -> 'possible for at least one person' suffices; no separation -> cannot rule out an idiosyncratic subject, so more are needed.
n_subjects_rule.freeze_point: after the pilot (2.8), BEFORE any confirmatory datum is collected
n_subjects_rule.record: write the frozen n into this file and record the date and commit hash in notes.md
n_subjects_rule.pilot_not_reused: the pilot subject (the researcher) is NOT reused in the confirmatory sample
n_subjects_rule.no_replacement: subjects removed by the eligibility gate (2.9) are NOT replaced; the reduced n is reported as-is
n_subjects_rule.multiplicity: Under the null, P(at least 1 of 5 independent subjects has p<0.05) = 1-0.95^5 = 23%. Across-subject multiplicity is handled ONLY by Fisher combination (3.3-1). 'One subject was significant' is never reported as evidence of separation.

design.optional_stopping: FORBIDDEN: no confirmatory analysis is viewed until the frozen n is collected; n is not changed on interim results; adding subjects until significance is explicitly forbidden

topic_condition_counterbalance.problem: If topics 1-4 are always LO and 5-8 always HI, condition is perfectly confounded with topic WITHIN each subject. Separation could then be 'topics 5-8 happened to be harder to write', which is the same class of error that led 2.2 to reject vocabulary constraints.
topic_condition_counterbalance.rule: All 8 topics exist in BOTH an LO and an HI version. Each subject sees each topic exactly once, in exactly one version (8 blocks = 8 topics).
topic_condition_counterbalance.within_person: IRREDUCIBLE: showing the same topic in both conditions would introduce a familiarity confound instead.
topic_condition_counterbalance.across_person: Two arrangements only. A: topics 1-4 = HI, 5-8 = LO. B: topics 5-8 = HI, 1-4 = LO. Subjects alternate A/B in subject-number order, generated deterministically by assign.py from SEED.
topic_condition_counterbalance.why_sufficient: Topic-driven artefacts point in OPPOSITE directions under A and B, so they do not accumulate under Fisher combination.
topic_condition_counterbalance.limitation: With odd n the arrangements are unbalanced; the per-arrangement counts MUST be reported. With n=1 no counterbalancing exists and topic confounding is NOT excluded - this must be stated explicitly in the report.

P-1.layout: copy / LO / HI / copy (HI-LO order seed-randomized)
checks: keystroke yield in BOTH conditions (feeds the 2.9 eligibility gate)
do the materials and the procedure work
known_deviations_from_the_confirmatory_d: the SAME topic appears in both conditions for the same person (2.7 forbids this in the confirmatory design; the second block is contaminated by familiarity)
C(2,1)=2 permutations cannot reach p<0.05, so NO test is run
with a single HI/LO pair the forced-comparison chain (2.6) does not exist, so NO manipulation check is taken
P-1.claims_allowed: keystroke volume and procedure only; nothing about separation

P-2.materials_needed: 8 topics x 2 versions + copy (written after P-1)
checks: early read on separation (NOT a verdict)

pilot.why_excluded: the researcher authored the task materials and knows both the hypothesis and the decision criteria
purposes: check that a 5-minute block yields enough keystrokes in BOTH conditions (feeds 2.9)
check that the materials and the procedure work
an early read on whether separation is plausible (NOT a verdict)
pilot.what_may_not_change_after_the_pilot: section 3 decision criteria. If they are changed, say so explicitly and forfeit the confirmatory status of that run (report as exploratory).
pilot.blinding: IMPOSSIBLE for the pilot (the researcher authored the materials). protocol.md documents a procedure for using the materials without pre-reading them, and the impossibility of full blinding MUST be stated in the report.
pilot.results_path: results/pilot/ (kept separate from the confirmatory analysis)

block_eligibility_gate.why: P014-type recurrence: a session with only 9 presses exists in the Phase1 cohort. A 5-minute HI block spent mostly reading degenerates the block features, and this happens SYSTEMATICALLY MORE OFTEN under HI. Dropping such a block would break the HI4/LO4 balance and therefore the C(8,4)=70 permutation structure; keeping it means the classifier separates 'typed vs did not type'.
block_eligibility_gate.unit: SUBJECT, not block. Blocks are never dropped.
block_eligibility_gate.primary_analysis: a subject with ANY of the 8 G1 blocks below the threshold is not analysed for the primary verdict (3.3)
block_eligibility_gate.positive_control: a subject with ANY of the 10 blocks below the threshold is not analysed for the positive control (2.5)
block_eligibility_gate.data_retained: ineligible subjects are NOT discarded; they are reported as ineligible together with their per-block keydown counts
block_eligibility_gate.justification_for_100: Phase1 natural argumentative logs (P010-P014, 360 consecutive 5-minute windows) have a median of 261 keydowns per 5-minute window and a first quartile of 61. 100 is roughly one sixth of the median: low enough not to disqualify slow writers, high enough to catch the P014 case (9 presses). Below 100 keydowns the Tier 1 quantiles (silence_p90, burst_p90) rest on a handful of values and carry no distributional meaning. A supervised 5-minute writing block should be denser than a natural log window, so this threshold is set at a 'should be met trivially' level.
block_eligibility_gate.frozen_before_pilot: the value is declared BEFORE the pilot and is NOT moved by the pilot result
block_eligibility_gate.why_not_a_researcher_degree_of_freedom: The gate is evaluated on keystroke counts alone, BEFORE any model is fitted. analyze.py enforces this ordering and prints eligibility before fitting, so 'drop subjects after seeing the result' is structurally impossible.

FS_A.block_aggregation: MEDIAN over the block's 1 Hz `feat` NDJSON rows
FS_A.source: the `feat` rows emitted by the running system, NOT recomputed from key events
FS_A.source_rationale: FS_A asks whether the LEGACY OBSERVATION SPACE separates the conditions, and that observation space is literally what the runtime computes. Recomputation offline would differ: InputEvent.is_repeat is not present in the NDJSON, and features.rs excludes auto-repeat from F1 and F4, so an offline recomputation would silently include auto-repeat and be a different quantity.
FS_A.status: GAP-FILL declared before any data exists. See .steering/20260802-g1-implementation/decisions.md D-2.

tier1_definitions.iki_ms: interval between consecutive keydowns; block measurement starts at first keydown and ends at last keydown (pre-block waiting time excluded)
tier1_definitions.silence: IKI >= 2000 ms (matches the current F5 threshold)
tier1_definitions.silence_p50_p90_max: quantiles/max of silence DURATIONS (ms) within the block; if the block contains zero silences all three are 0 (declared, not missing)
tier1_definitions.burst: run of consecutive keystrokes delimited by silences; burst length = number of keystrokes in the run
tier1_definitions.burst_p50_p90: quantiles of burst LENGTH within the block
tier1_definitions.band_rates_excluded: the banded silence rates of personalization-and-online-learning.md 5.2 are NOT used here: >120s band cannot occur in a 5-minute block, and adding features would worsen the 14-features / ~6-training-blocks ratio. Deferred to Phase2.

offline_computability.claim: ALL of Tier0 and Tier1 are computable offline from the existing anonymized NDJSON. The version-1 claim that schema_dto.rs must be unfrozen first was WRONG.

evidence.keys_and_bs_rate_and_silence_and_burst: `key` rows carry one record per keystroke: {t, category, press} after anonymization (analysis/anonymize.rs converts vk -> category and absolute epoch t -> session-relative ms)

offline_computability.what_is_actually_frozen: wiring Tier0/1 into the RUNTIME inference path (the `feat` row and the HMM). That is irrelevant to offline analysis.
offline_computability.consequence: G1 has no technical dependency on lifting the Phase1 freeze; analysis touches zero lines of src-tauri/. Whether to RUN it before the freeze is lifted remains a researcher decision (ADR-009 D7 states G1 is the first task after unfreezing).

platform_availability.ime_dwell_med: ime_shadow is emitted only under #[cfg(target_os = "windows")] (lib.rs). On macOS this feature is STRUCTURALLY MISSING and is 0 in every block.
platform_availability.external_paste_chars: with paper-handout materials (protocol.md) no paste occurs, so this feature is 0 in every block
platform_availability.recommendation: running on Windows 11 lets FS_B be evaluated with all 14 features as designed. This is a RECOMMENDATION, not a decision criterion.

degenerate_feature_handling.rule: A feature whose standard deviation is 0 within a training fold is standardized to 0 in that fold (it contributes nothing).
degenerate_feature_handling.not_removed: The feature set is NOT changed. FS_B remains 14 features (section 3.2 is untouched).
degenerate_feature_handling.mandatory_reporting: Which features degenerated, and in how many folds, MUST appear in the output (`degenerate_features`). Never pass silently.
degenerate_feature_handling.os_reporting: The execution OS is recorded in env.md and in the results. If ime_dwell_med was missing on macOS, report that FS_B was effectively evaluated with 13 features.

analysis.rationale_for_penalization: With 8 blocks per subject, each training fold has ~6 blocks while FS_B has 14 features. Unpenalized logistic regression would hit complete separation, producing diverging coefficients and artificially high AUC that cannot be distinguished from real signal. A fixed-strength L2 penalty guarantees finite coefficients. Strength is PRESPECIFIED, not tuned: tuning would require nested CV that 6 training blocks cannot support. See [V63] (penalized methods help when events are few).
analysis.known_limitation: lambda=1.0 on z-scored features is a convention, not an optimum. It is frozen before data collection so that it cannot be chosen to favour a result.

permutation_test.why_primary: The ENTIRE pipeline (standardization, penalized fit, CV, AUC) is re-run on each permuted label assignment. Any optimism from small-sample fitting inflates AUC under permuted labels too, so it is absorbed by the null distribution. This is what makes the result trustworthy despite the small block count.
permutation_test.fisher_known_limitation: Within-subject p-values are discrete (minimum 1/70 = 0.0143, finitely many attainable values), so they deviate from the uniform null Fisher assumes. This discreteness makes the combined p CONSERVATIVE (harder to reach significance), not anti-conservative. Frozen knowingly.
permutation_test.enumeration: EXHAUSTIVE, never sampled. G1: all C(8,4)=70 label assignments. Positive control: all C(10,2)=45. Therefore the permutation test is SEED-INDEPENDENT.
permutation_test.fisher_applies_when: n>=2 only. With n=1 the single within-subject p is reported as-is (combining one p-value with Fisher would not return the same number and would only cause confusion).
permutation_test.cross_validation_fold_definition: leave-one-block-pair-out: every (held-out positive block, held-out negative block) pair is one fold. G1: 4x4=16 folds. Positive control: 2x8=16 folds. The out-of-fold AUC is the fraction of folds in which the held-out positive block scores higher than the held-out negative block (ties count 0.5). This IS the AUC over held-out pairs.
permutation_test.fold_definition_status: GAP-FILL: the frozen version-1 text specified 'within-subject leave-one-block-pair-out' and 'out-of-fold AUC' but not how folds are aggregated. Declared here before any data exists. See .steering/20260802-g1-implementation/decisions.md D-3.

descriptive_thresholds.note: Secondary. Computed out-of-fold. Used to judge practical magnitude, NOT significance.
descriptive_thresholds.per_subject_auc_min_fraction_denominator: ceil(0.8 * n), where n is the value frozen after the pilot. Version 1 said 'n=5 -> at least 4 subjects'; expressing it as a fraction is a CLARIFICATION ONLY - neither 0.8 nor 0.6 changed.
descriptive_thresholds.n_equals_1_note: The descriptive criteria still apply with n=1 (median = that subject's AUC, fraction = 1/1), but the report MUST state that passing them carries little practical meaning at n=1.

prespecified_thresholds.justification_for_0_70: Phase1 observed chance-level for current features (0.442-0.507) and 0.60-0.68 for the strongest simple signal (keys->Q2). A deliberately induced high-friction condition must exceed the best naturally observed weak signal.

separation_diagnostic.note: If perfect training separation still occurs under the fixed L2 penalty, report it. Do not silently pass.

manipulation_check.reason_not_in_app: probe_scheduler.rs is frozen; also 1-5 Likert caused straight-lining in Phase1 (P013)
manipulation_check.asked_for_blocks: G1 blocks 3..9 only (7 comparisons); NOT asked for copy blocks nor for the first G1 block (no valid predecessor)
manipulation_check.denominator: ONLY cross-condition pairs (HI vs LO). Same-condition pairs (HI-HI, LO-LO) carry no information and are excluded from the denominator.

prespecified_exclusions.subject_level: none_post_hoc; only pre-declared consent withdrawal, plus the pre-declared eligibility gate in design.block_eligibility_gate (evaluated on keystroke counts BEFORE any model is fitted, never replaced)
prespecified_exclusions.block_level: only technical log loss (keystroke log missing or truncated); rule frozen before data collection. Blocks are NEVER dropped for low keystroke count - that is handled at subject level to preserve the HI4/LO4 permutation structure.

asymmetry_of_conclusions.why: Argumentative writing is the BEST CASE for keystroke observation (see design.domain_rationale), so a negative result travels further than a positive one.
asymmetry_of_conclusions.negative_result_scope: A negative result (with the positive control passing) is negative evidence about KEYSTROKES AS AN INSTRUMENT and applies to ALL domains: losing on the densest typing ground means the thinner VibeCoding and Creative grounds cannot win.
negative_result_next_actions: doubt the axis itself; do not build the pipeline (personalization-and-online-learning.md 8.2 G1)
move instrumentation resources to Adapter B (coding events: accept / reject / test / revert), i.e. content-free events that are NOT keystrokes
asymmetry_of_conclusions.negative_result_caveat: Never state 'keystrokes cannot measure this in principle'. [P44] leaves 'the manipulation was too subtle' open.
asymmetry_of_conclusions.positive_result_scope: A positive result licenses ONLY 'separable in argumentative writing'. It does NOT transfer to other domains (ADR-001 states this explicitly) and does NOT imply 'work state is separable during real work' (see ecological_validity).
asymmetry_of_conclusions.overclaiming_forbidden: Do not generalize a pass into 'the GSE observation space was sufficient'.

ecological_validity.statement: G1 does NOT measure whether real work states are separable. It is the prior question: a FLOOR CHECK on measurability of a contrast the experimenter deliberately created.
limits: condition labels are assigned by the experimenter, not felt friction; the manipulation check only guarantees subjective ORDER
tasks are cut into 5-minute blocks, while real stalling can span tens of minutes to days
supervised, with given materials and a specified output length; not self-directed work
fixed to argumentative writing, which participant P011 stated they rarely do continuously
the copy positive control is position-fixed and therefore confounded with position; no effect size is claimed
ecological_validity.consequence: A pass does NOT imply separability in natural work logs. Phase1 failed that separately (GATE3 DataInsufficient) and a G1 pass does not retroactively resolve it.

forbidden_post_hoc: changing n after seeing interim results
reusing task material sets across sessions

scripts.assign.py: deterministic per-subject assignment (arrangement A/B, topic->condition, ABBA-balanced then seed-randomized block order)
scripts.validate_materials.py: mechanical checks on the task materials (source count, matched total length, stated output requirement)
scripts.analyze.py: block features (FS_A from feat rows, Tier0/1 from key/paste/ime_shadow rows) + the frozen decision pipeline
scripts.run.sh: pre-execution readiness check: green when materials, protocol and consent are all present and valid; red otherwise

reproducibility.permutation_seed_independence: the permutation test enumerates all assignments exhaustively, so it does not depend on SEED
reproducibility.dependencies: Python standard library only; no requirements.txt (same policy as experiments/20260802-within-person-scope-detector)

prereg.note: G1 is a new gate introduced after the v0.3 preregistration was frozen. It is now separately preregistered in preregistration.md (frozen before any data).

preregistration.authority: preregistration.md is authoritative if it disagrees with this file
preregistration.note: G1 is NOT covered by docs/preregistration-v0.3.md (frozen Phase1 contract, unchanged). Preregistered separately.

positive_control.purpose: Make the FS-A x / FS-B x cell interpretable by separating 'keystrokes cannot measure work state' from 'manipulation too weak' and 'instrument broken'.
positive_control.known_detectability: copy-typing vs authentic writing is separable from keystroke logs alone (RF 99% [P37]); revisions move across tasks [P36]
positive_control.test: same pipeline as the primary analysis (standardization, L2 fit, CV, AUC, permutation)

decision_rule.pass_and_hi_lo_fails: ONLY case in which 'keystrokes cannot separate friction' may be claimed; must also state that the manipulation may have been too subtle [P44]
decision_rule.fail: G1 IS VOID. Instrument/pipeline fault suspected. Do not read x/x as a property of the world. Diagnose and re-run.

positive_control.known_limitation: Copy blocks are at FIXED positions, so this separation is confounded with position. Use as a FLOOR CHECK on instrument health only; do NOT claim an effect size and do NOT cite this test as evidence of effect. Also, copy vs writing is a much larger contrast than HI/LO: passing does not guarantee power for HI/LO.

production_confound.why: [P43] reports lower text production rate for integrated tasks. FS_B contains `keys`. Separation could therefore be attributable to output-volume differences rather than friction - the same objection used to reject vocabulary constraints in README 2.2.
mandatory_reporting: per-condition realised output (block `keys` and final character count)
standardized coefficients of each FS_B feature
out-of-fold AUC of `keys` ALONE (single feature, descriptive)
production_confound.interpretation_rule: If FS_B AUC does not substantially exceed the `keys`-alone AUC, the separation may be attributable to output volume and must be reported as such.
production_confound.not_a_third_feature_set: The keys-alone AUC is a descriptive single-feature statistic, NOT a third feature set. It does not violate the forbidden_post_hoc rule.

prior_work.finding: Prior controlled protocols EXIST and their results are INCONSISTENT.
prior_work.same_family_manipulation: integrated (reading-into-writing / source-based) vs independent writing task, e.g. TOEFL iBT
prior_work.P43_chan_2017: N=2, exploratory: integrated more demanding - longer pauses, more revisions, lower production rate
prior_work.P44_michel_et_al_2020: N=60, TOEFL iBT 2 independent x 2 integrated, counterbalanced, with eye-tracking: apart from source use, writing behaviours and cognitive processes were largely SIMILAR across task types
consequences: do not claim the manipulation is our own invention
a null result is realistic and is declared valuable in advance (preregistration.md 3.7)
the x/x cell is not interpretable without the positive control -> positive_control added
prior_work.directional_prior_from_P36: mean IKI stable across tasks; revisions / word count / total time move -> predicts FS_A fail, FS_B pass. NOT a decision criterion; recorded so that a mismatch cannot later be called 'expected'.
